claim:
Text: "In a letter to Steve Jobs, Sean Connery refused to appear in an apple commercial."
Claim date: October 31, 2020
before_justification: The alleged letter from Sean Connery to Steve Jobs rejecting an Apple commercial is a fabrication, originating from the satirical website Scoopertino and never actually sent. Multiple reputable sources, including [Business Insider](https://www.businessinsider.com/james-bond-sean-connery-steve-jobs-apple-letter-2011-6), [Snopes](https://www.snopes.com/fact-check/false-sean-connery-letter-to-apple/), [CNET](https://www.cnet.com/culture/fake-sean-connery-letter-to-steve-jobs-goes-viral/), and the [Daily Mail](https://www.dailymail.co.uk/news/article-2006317/Sean-Connery-letter-Steve-Jobs-rejecting-offer-appear-Apple-ad-revealed-fake.html), confirm the letter is fake and that Sean Connery never appeared in any Apple commercial. There is no verifiable evidence of any such correspondence or refusal.
after_justification: The claim is **refuted**. While some sources mention a letter from Sean Connery to Steve Jobs declining an Apple commercial, a CNET investigation explicitly labeled the letter as a fake that went viral [source](https://www.cnet.com/culture/fake-sean-connery-letter-to-steve-jobs-goes-viral/). This debunking by a reputable tech news outlet is the most authoritative evidence, outweighing secondary references that lack verifiable primary sources like a scan or authenticated archive entry.

Therefore, the available information is insufficient to confirm the specific claim about a letter.
